name: Rittenhouse Square
tagline: A leafy park ringed by the city's best cafes and brownstones
description: Rittenhouse is Philadelphia at its most polished: a small formal park surrounded by brownstones, mid-century towers, indie bookshops and a heavy concentration of coffee shops. Walk Street and Sansom Street carry the restaurants. Almost everything downtown, including three co-working buildings, is within a fifteen minute walk.
bestFor: Nomads who want zero car dependence and a cafe on every corner.
pros: Best walk score in the city, transit and rail close
Park, gyms and grocery all within a few blocks
cons: Street noise and sirens on the main corridors
Parking is expensive and scarce if you drive

name: Fishtown
tagline: Old rowhouses turned into breweries, record bars and coffee roasters
description: A former working class riverside district north of Center City, Fishtown is narrow rowhouse streets with Frankford Avenue running through as a strip of breweries, music venues, roasters and new build condos. The population skews young, and the Market-Frankford El puts Center City about ten minutes away.
bestFor: Younger nomads who want nightlife, music and a strong cafe culture on their doorstep.
pros: Excellent third wave coffee and brewery scene
El train reaches Center City in around ten minutes
Still cheaper to rent than Center City proper
cons: Weekend bar noise carries into residential blocks
Rapid gentrification has pushed prices up fast
Very tight street parking and narrow one way streets

name: East Passyunk
tagline: South Philly rowhouses around a diagonal restaurant avenue
description: East Passyunk Avenue cuts diagonally through the South Philly grid and is lined with BYOB restaurants, cafes and old Italian bakeries, with the Singing Fountain as its centre. Behind it sit tight blocks of two storey rowhouses, part long time Italian American families, part younger arrivals.
bestFor: Nomads who want an authentic neighborhood feel with a serious food scene.
pros: One of the strongest restaurant strips in the city
Broad Street Line subway is a short walk away
cons: A 25 to 30 minute trip to Center City by transit
Row homes are small with almost no outdoor space
Street parking competition is genuinely brutal

name: University City
tagline: Penn and Drexel campuses with the cheapest central rooms
description: West of the Schuylkill, University City is dominated by Penn and Drexel, with Victorian twins on the side streets and modern towers along Market and Chestnut. Baltimore Avenue keeps the cheaper cafes and co-ops. It has the most student sublets in the city, which makes short furnished stays easy to find.
bestFor: Budget nomads who want cheap furnished sublets close to the centre.
pros: Cheap short term sublets, especially over summer
30th Street Station for regional and Amtrak trains
Bike friendly with flat routes into Center City
cons: Quality drops off quickly on the western edges
Property crime and bike theft are common near campus
Empties out and feels flat during university breaks

name: Northern Liberties
tagline: Loft conversions and beer gardens on a quieter grid
description: An old industrial district turned residential, Northern Liberties mixes converted warehouse lofts, new low rise condos and the Piazza plaza with beer gardens and small galleries. It is calmer and more spread out than Fishtown next door, and the walk or bike into Old City takes about fifteen minutes.
bestFor: Remote workers who want a modern apartment and quiet weeknights near the centre.
pros: Modern loft and condo stock with real workspace
Quieter weeknights than Fishtown or Old City
Easy walk or bike into Old City and Center City
cons: Fewer everyday shops than older neighborhoods
New build rents are close to Center City levels
Some blocks still feel empty and under construction
